blockers.summary: Obtain qualified review of the complete dependency and notice boundary, including the retained optional sharp/libvips installation model.

Review and approve the provenance of the official Maps palette, stops, and rail grammar before publication; document the independently authored Tileflow boundary or replace any calibration whose provenance cannot be established.

Audit the three current organization members and enable organization-wide 2FA without removing an operator. The repository ruleset and npm-publish required-reviewer gate are configured, but organization 2FA is not yet enforced.

Merge the reviewed manual-only publish.yml into protected main, verify the live GitHub workflow exposes only workflow_dispatch, and only then re-enable the Publish workflow. The legacy scheduled workflow is deliberately disabled during this transition.

Validate the approved complete World v1 public descriptor and producer-observed data contract with a real release: exact archive and descriptor hashes, encoding, zooms, bounds, schema fields, attribution, immutable tile URLs, current resolution, and rollback. No development fixture or placeholder value may be used.

Merge and deploy Hosted's canonical create-only base-asset publisher and verified /base/<assetSetSha256>/glyph delivery; provision its scoped R2 credentials; publish and read back official set 33d4de5e8086d9d629d67d3f39fedb87e23686c4c1ac653c27e2a52aee9d00b3 including licenses; then change every URL-backed official root—Streets, Ferraris, Härad, Soundings, and Verdant—from the mutable /fonts URL to that exact URL and rerun visual and packed-package validation.

Bootstrap @tileflow/maps and @tileflow/interactions once as public npm packages from reviewed bootstrap-only versions under the non-default bootstrap tag, preserving each package's catalog initialVersion for its first protected alpha. Then configure each Trusted Publisher for tileflow/tileflow-sdk, workflow publish.yml, environment npm-publish, and allowed action npm publish.
Run the complete source, package, clean-consumer, browser/framework, and publication-free release validation described in PUBLISHING.md on the exact candidate commit.
